subject: Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data

messages.author: 937253792853878c
messages.subject: Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data
parts:
Dear Stan users,


I am trying to fit a Compound Poisson-Gamma model (also known as Tweedie distribution) for zero-inflated continuous data. I have a BUGS model script which works fine, but I wasn’t able to translate it in Stan. I am new to Stan so I used the Hurdle model example in the manual as a basis for my Stan code.


I run the model from R using Rstan. I have attached an R script which generates an artificial dataset and perform inferences with Stan and JAGS.


When I run my model with Rstan I am getting a non-fatal warning for using increment_log_prob() for the statement ngis[s] ~ poisson(…).


But I think that the main error comes from the gamma part where I get the following error:  

Exception thrown at line 38: stan::math::gamma_log: Shape parameter is 0, but must be >0!

It seems like the truncation of the Poisson distribution is not working and produces zeros, where it should be strictly positive integers. I tried to uninstall and re-install Rstan but nothing changed and I don’t really see how I can fix my Stan code. My Stan code is:

data {
int<lower=0> n_obs;
real<lower=0> SV[n_obs];
real<lower=0> Y[n_obs];
}

parameters {
real mu;
real<lower=0> rho_a;
real<lower=0> rho_b;
}

transformed parameters {
real <lower=0> lambda[n_obs];
real<lower=0, upper=1>  proba[n_obs];

  for (s in 1:n_obs){
    lambda[s] <-  exp(mu)*SV[s];
    proba[s] <- 1 - exp(-lambda[s]);
  }

}

model {

int ngis[n_obs];

// Priors
rho_a ~ gamma(0.01, 0.01);
rho_b ~ gamma(0.01, 0.01);
mu ~ normal(0, 10);

//Observation model
for (s in 1:n_obs){
  (Y[s] == 0) ~ bernoulli(proba[s]);
 
  if (Y[s] > 0)
    ngis[s] ~ poisson(lambda[s])T[1,];
    Y[s] ~ gamma(ngis[s]*rho_a, rho_b);
  }
}



I would be grateful for any advice to run this model properly.


Many thanks,


Jean-Baptiste

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data
parts:
This

> int ngis[n_obs];

declares a local variable which is never defined before it used
here:

Stan doesn't work this way --- the ~ doesn't do a random number
generation. Nor does it define a graphical model the way BUGS does.
It just increments the log density with the value of the probability
function at the argument. If the arguments are undefined, so is the
result.

One thing Stan can't do is latent Poisson variables. So if everything
hinges on that, then you won't be able to use Stan. Usually these
models go the other way around, though, with a continuous mixture.

So it looks like the Tweedie distribution is going to be beyond
Stan's ability to model as is; here's what the Wikipedia says:

In probability and statistics, the Tweedie distributions are a family of probability
distributions which include the purely continuous normal and gamma distributions,
the purely discrete scaled Poisson distribution, and the class of mixed compound
Poisson–gamma distributions which have positive mass at zero, but are otherwise continuous.

The only way it'd be possible is if ngis could be analytically marginalized out.

- Bob

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Compound Poisson-Gamma model for zero-inflated continuous data
parts:
If there's a problem with too large values for a parameter alpha,
it's often possible to parameterize as 1 / alpha. For example, we
typically use scale for parameterizing a normal, not precision, with
a prior with support at zero like a half-Cauchy.

- Bob
